title: Freedom from Condemnation
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Freedom from condemnation means that those who are in Christ Jesus are no longer under God’s condemning judgment. The believer’s guilt has been answered by Christ, and no final accusation can overturn God’s verdict.
summary: Freedom from condemnation means that those who are in Christ Jesus are no longer under God’s condemning judgment. The believer’s guilt has been answered by Christ, and no final accusation can overturn God’s verdict.
christFocus: Jesus Christ bore condemnation for His people so they might be justified and free. In Him, the guilty are forgiven, declared righteous, and released from the sentence sin deserved.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Condemnation is the righteous judgment sinners deserve before God. Scripture does not deny guilt or soften sin. It announces that in Christ there is now no condemnation.

This freedom exists because Christ dealt with sin. He bore the curse, canceled the record of debt, and satisfied the righteous requirement that sinners could never fulfill.

Freedom from condemnation is not the same as freedom from discipline, conviction, or repentance. God still corrects His children, but He does not condemn them as enemies.

This doctrine gives the believer courage to come into the light. Because final condemnation has been removed in Christ, sin can be confessed honestly and fought faithfully.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people confuse conviction with condemnation. Conviction draws believers toward repentance and Christ; condemnation tells them to hide in hopelessness. This doctrine helps them discern the difference.

For those crushed by shame, freedom from condemnation is life-giving. Their sins were serious, but Christ’s work is sufficient. God’s verdict in Christ stands above every accusation.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When condemnation rises, answer it with the Gospel. Do not hide sin, excuse sin, or live under hopeless accusation. Confess, repent, and return to Christ, trusting that there is no condemnation for those who are in Him.
